title: VIDEO- Why Danger Symbols Can't Last Forever with Vox

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars, and this is a video episode that we made with Vox.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯，这是我们与Vox合作制作的一期视频节目。

sentences.en: So, if you haven't already, turn on your screen and look at it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你还没这么做，请打开屏幕并看着它。

sentences.en: It'll make much more sense that way.
sentences.zh: 这样看会更容易理解。

sentences.en: You probably know how this symbol is supposed to make you feel.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道这个符号本该让你产生什么样的感觉。

sentences.en: And this one.
sentences.zh: 还有这个。

sentences.en: This one, too, even if you're not exactly sure what it means.
sentences.zh: 这个也是，即使你并不完全确定它是什么意思。

sentences.en: But what about this?
sentences.zh: 但这个呢？

sentences.en: This symbol, the Jolly Roger, was once one of the most feared symbols in the world.
sentences.zh: 这个符号，海盗旗，曾经是世界上最令人恐惧的符号之一。

sentences.en: It represented death, pirates, and poison.
sentences.zh: 它代表着死亡、海盗和剧毒。

sentences.en: But today, it's associated more with treasure, blockbuster movies, or Halloween than actual danger.
sentences.zh: 但今天，它更多地与宝藏、大片或万圣节联系在一起，而不是真正的危险。

sentences.en: We are surrounded by icons that warn us.
sentences.zh: 我们周围充斥着警告我们的图标。

sentences.en: What to stay away from.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们远离什么。

sentences.en: What not to do.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们不要做什么。

sentences.en: What to be afraid of.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们应该害怕什么。

sentences.en: But how do you design a symbol in a way that will last across generations and languages?
sentences.zh: 但是，你该如何设计一个能跨越世代和语言的符号呢？

sentences.en: It turns out that is an incredibly hard thing to do.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这是一件极其困难的事情。

sentences.en: Back in the early 20th century, there was an urgent need for a new kind of warning symbol.
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪初，人们就迫切需要一种新型的警告符号。

sentences.en: At the time, there was no universal standard for communicating the presence of dangerous biological materials.
sentences.zh: 当时，对于如何传达危险生物材料的存在，还没有通用的标准。

sentences.en: Laboratories at the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国陆军的实验室使用一个倒置的蓝色三角形。

sentences.en: Army used an inverted blue triangle.
sentences.zh: 海军的实验室使用一个粉红色的矩形。

sentences.en: Those at the Navy used a pink rectangle.
sentences.zh: 万国邮政联盟使用紫色背景上的白色手杖和蛇。

sentences.en: The Universal Postal Convention used a white staff and snake on a violet background.
sentences.zh: 在传达风险的视觉语言上，没有任何一致性。

sentences.en: There was no consistency in the visual language used to communicate risk.
sentences.zh: 这很危险，可能会导致意外感染。

sentences.en: That was dangerous and could lead to accidental infections.
sentences.zh: 因此在1966年，陶氏化学的一组工程师和设计师着手为生物危害材料创造一个尽可能好的图标。

sentences.en: So in 1966, a group of engineers and designers at Dow Chemical set out to create the best possible icon for biohazardous materials.
sentences.zh: 他们提出了六项设计标准。

sentences.en: They laid out six design criteria.
sentences.zh: 首先，它需要视觉上引人注目，以便立即引起注意。

sentences.en: First, it needed to be visually striking so that it would draw immediate attention.
sentences.zh: 这排除了海军和陆军使用的那些简单形状。

sentences.en: That ruled out simple shapes like those from the Navy and Army.
sentences.zh: 它还必须是独特且明确的，以免与用于其他目的的符号混淆。

sentences.en: It also had to be unique and unambiguous in order not to be confused with symbols used for other purposes.
sentences.zh: 这排除了蛇和手杖，因为它们有多个版本，而且作为医学的通用符号，含义相当模糊。

sentences.en: That ruled out the snake and staff, which has multiple versions and has a pretty vague meaning as a general symbol for medicine.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，它必须易于识别和记忆。

sentences.en: On top of that, it had to be quickly recognizable and easily recalled.
sentences.zh: 它必须易于模版印刷，并且具有旋转对称性，以便从各个角度看起来都一样。

sentences.en: It had to be easy to stencil and rotationally symmetrical in order to appear identical from all angles.
sentences.zh: 最后，它必须能被各种背景的群体所接受。

sentences.en: And lastly, it had to be acceptable to groups of all backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 于是，陶氏化学团队设计了一个实验。

sentences.en: So the Dow Chemical team designed an experiment.
sentences.zh: 该实验背后的环境健康工程师查尔斯·鲍德温说，团队想要一些令人难忘但又没有特定含义的东西，这样我们就可以教育人们它代表什么。

sentences.en: Charles Baldwin, an environmental health engineer behind the experiment,
sentences.zh: 他们向来自25个美国城市的300人展示了一组24个符号。

sentences.en: said that the team wanted something that was memorable but meaningless so we could educate people as to what it means.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个新设计的生物危害标志和18个常见符号。

sentences.en: They showed a set of 24 symbols to 300 people from 25 American cities.
sentences.zh: 比如花生先生、德士古之星、壳牌石油标志、红十字会和一个纳粹万字旗。

sentences.en: There were six newly designed biohazard markers and 18 common symbols.
sentences.zh: 参与者被要求猜测每一个符号的含义，这被用来给每个符号赋予一个“意义得分”。

sentences.en: Things like Mr. Peanut, the Texaco star, the Shell Oil symbol, the Red Cross, and a swastika.
sentences.zh: 一周后，同样的参与者被展示了那最初的24个符号，外加36个新符号。

sentences.en: Participants were asked to guess the meaning of each one, which was used to assign each one a meaningfulness score.
sentences.zh: 他们被要求识别出哪些符号是他们在研究的第一轮中看到过的。

sentences.en: A week later, the same participants were shown those original 24 symbols plus 36 more.
sentences.zh: 在六个竞争的生物危害设计中，这一个脱颖而出。

sentences.en: They were asked to identify which symbols they remembered seeing in the previous round of the study.
sentences.zh: 它的记忆度得分最高，但意义得分最低。

sentences.en: Among the six competing biohazard designs, this one stood out.
sentences.zh: 所以它令人难忘，但也为那些想赋予它意义的设计师提供了一张完全空白的画布。

sentences.en: It scored the highest in memorability, but the lowest in meaningfulness.
sentences.zh: 就这样，它成为了国家标准。

sentences.en: So it was unforgettable, but also a totally blank slate for designers who wanted to give it meaning.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易忽略这些符号在视觉传达方面所做的工作有多大。

sentences.en: And with that, it became a national standard.
sentences.zh: 它们很简单。

sentences.en: It's easy to overlook how much visual communication work these symbols are doing.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一把直尺和一个圆规就能重现它们。

sentences.en: They're simple.
sentences.zh: 而且与其他大多数危险符号不同，它们并不指代现有的物理对象或概念。

sentences.en: You'll need a straight edge and a compass to recreate them.
sentences.zh: 但几十年来，它们一直保持着标志性的地位，帮助人们识别那些可能在未来几千年里依然构成威胁的严重危险。

sentences.en: And unlike most other hazard symbols, they don't reference an existing physical object or idea.
sentences.zh: 这就提出了一个问题：这些符号的含义能经受住时间的考验吗？

sentences.en: But they've remained iconic for decades, helping people recognize serious dangers that may remain a threat for thousands of years to come.
sentences.zh: 很少有人像格雷戈里·本福德那样深入思考过这个问题。

sentences.en: And that raises the question, could the meaning of those symbols stand the test of time?
sentences.zh: 他是一位物理学家和科幻小说作家。

sentences.en: Few people have pondered that question quite like Gregory Benford.
sentences.zh: 20世纪90年代，他受邀参与“废物隔离试验工厂”（WIP）项目。

sentences.en: He's a physicist and science fiction author.
sentences.zh: WIP是由美国能源部组织的一个位于新墨西哥州东南部平原的放射性废物大型储存点。

sentences.en: And in the 1990s, he was invited to work on the Waste Isolation Pilot Project, or WIP.
sentences.zh: 本福德被请来帮助计算在放射性废物保持危险的这段时间内，有人或有东西闯入该地点的概率。

sentences.en: The WIP is a massive storage site for radioactive waste in the southeastern plains of New Mexico, organized by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 大约是未来1万年。

sentences.en: Department of Energy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，随便举个例子。

sentences.en: Benford was brought on to help calculate the probability that someone or something would intrude on the site for as long as it remains dangerous.
sentences.zh: 记录最久的可能就是天主教会或犹太教的核心，这告诉了我们什么才是真正持久的东西。

sentences.en: Approximately the next 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 符号的含义会随时间改变，就像海盗旗一样，它对WIP的放射性威胁不起作用。

sentences.en: Well, name anything.
sentences.zh: 如果你接近WIP设施，看到一个骷髅和交叉骨，你可能会想：

sentences.en: The record probably is something like the Catholic Church or the core of the Jewish religion, which tells us something about what really lasts.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这就是海盗埋藏宝藏的地方。

sentences.en: The meaning of a symbol can change over time, like the Jolly Roger, which wouldn't work for the radioactive threat at the WIP.
sentences.zh: 那么，如何跨越任何语言来标示一种长期存在的危险呢？

sentences.en: If you're approaching the WIP facility and you see a skull and crossbones, you might think,
sentences.zh: 自20世纪70年代以来，工程师、人类学家、物理学家和行为科学家针对这个问题提出了不同的解决方案。

sentences.en: Hey, this is where the pirates buried their treasure.
sentences.zh: 一种策略是为符号增加背景信息。

sentences.en: So how do you indicate a long-lasting danger across any language?
sentences.zh: 通过像这样用三格漫画来说明因果关系，即使符号失去了原本的含义，设计师也能传达出这个想法。

sentences.en: Since the 1970s, engineers, anthropologists, physicists, and behavioral scientists have proposed different solutions to that problem.
sentences.zh: 但这种视觉传达方式仍然对用户做了很多假设。

sentences.en: One strategy was to add context to the symbol.
sentences.zh: 假设他们会从左到右阅读，假设他们能理解画面之间的因果关系，

sentences.en: By illustrating cause and effect in a three-part cartoon like this, designers could communicate the idea even if the symbol lost its meaning.
sentences.zh: 当然，还假设图画本身能经受住几千年的磨损。

sentences.en: But this kind of visual communication still made a lot of assumptions about the user.
sentences.zh: 因此，其他设计师开始专注于通过改变地点本身的形状，在没有文字交流的情况下创造警告。

sentences.en: That they would read left to right, that they would understand causality between frames,
sentences.zh: 这产生了像这样的设计。

sentences.en: and, of course, that the drawing itself would last millennia of wear and tear.
sentences.zh: 尖刺场、禁区方块、巨型金字塔。

sentences.en: So other designers started to focus on creating a warning without inscribed communication by altering the shape of the location itself.
sentences.zh: 这些设计利用了人类对恐惧和不安的本能来让人远离。

sentences.en: And that yielded designs like this.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，它们也不是万无一失的。

sentences.en: Spike fields, forbidding blocks, giant pyramids.
sentences.zh: 设计师无法确定它们会被视为恐怖还是迷人。

sentences.en: These designs capitalized on natural instincts of fear and discomfort to keep people away.
sentences.zh: 这两种冲动之间存在冲突。

sentences.en: But even then, they weren't foolproof.
sentences.zh: 你希望人们注意到它，但你又不希望人们去那里。

sentences.en: Designers couldn't be sure whether they would be perceived as terrifying or fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这两者永远会相互抵触。

sentences.en: Conflict between these two urges.
sentences.zh: 所以，在没有符号、没有基本插图、没有物理结构的情况下，你该如何有效地传达警告呢？

sentences.en: You want people to notice it, but you don't want people to go there.
sentences.zh: 这就是更具哲学意义的设计方案发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: Those are always going to fight each other.
sentences.zh: 1984年，《德国符号学杂志》发表了一系列来自不同学者的解决方案。

sentences.en: So, without symbols, without basic illustrations, without physical structures, how can you effectively communicate a warning?
sentences.zh: 语言学家托马斯·西巴赫提议建立一个“原子祭司团”，

sentences.en: That's where the more philosophical design solutions come in.
sentences.zh: 由一个排他的政治团体利用其自身的仪式和神话来保存有关放射性区域的信息。

sentences.en: In 1984, the German Journal of Semiotics published a series of solutions from various scholars.
sentences.zh: 哲学家弗朗索瓦·巴斯蒂德和保罗·法布尔提议通过基因工程培育出生物发光猫，让它们在有放射性的地方发光。

sentences.en: Linguist Thomas Siebiach proposed creating an atomic priesthood,
sentences.zh: 通过创作关于发光猫危险性的歌曲和传统，

sentences.en: where an exclusive political group would use its own rituals and myths to preserve information about the radioactive areas.
sentences.zh: 这种警告可以像我们拥有的最古老的文明遗迹一样持久。

sentences.en: And philosophers Francoise Bastide and Paolo Fabre proposed to genetically engineer bioluminescent cats that would glow in the presence of radioactivity.
sentences.zh: 文化。

sentences.en: By creating songs and traditions about the danger of glowing cats,
sentences.zh: 对于警告遥远未来的人们，没有绝对的解决方案。

sentences.en: the warning could last as long as the oldest relics of civilization we have.
sentences.zh: 但设计清晰、包容的符号将继续是我们保障人们安全的基本组成部分。

sentences.en: Culture.
sentences.zh: 我们将发生变化，我们进行视觉交流的方式也会随之改变。

sentences.en: There's no definitive solution for warning people far into the future.
sentences.zh: 我们的警告符号也必须随我们一起改变。

sentences.en: But designing clear, inclusive symbols will continue to be a fundamental part of how we keep people safe.
sentences.zh: 那甚至不是这个想法。

sentences.en: We will change, and so will the ways we communicate visually.
sentences.zh: 我渴望贪婪。

sentences.en: Our warning symbols will just have to change along with us.
sentences.zh: 这是99%隐形。

sentences.en: That's not even this idea.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯，这是我们与Vox合作制作的一期视频节目。

sentences.zh: 所以，如果你还没这么做，请打开屏幕并看着它。
